system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The Seller’s assertions of “market standard”, principal-level agreement and “FINAL” status are not evidence of Buyer approval. Recommendations below are Buyer negotiating positions, not agreed terms. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been provided, so their wording and factual conclusions require verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recourse proportionate to the business risks, with separate treatment for protected categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, reserving the final position pending DD and recovery/security assessment; a 20% cap transfers substantial unidentified risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, related-claim aggregation and exclusions for protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related claims and excluding title, tax, fraud and specific indemnities; the proposed double threshold materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitation provisions extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer category-specific periods and effective claim-preservation mechanics. | **Counter at 24 months and reject blanket application**, preserving timely notified contingent claims and allowing reasonable time to commence proceedings; issues may emerge only after an annual reporting cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the general cap and time limit. | Separate warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, valid issuance and unencumbered transfer, with no thresholds or disclosure/knowledge dilution. | **Require a separate cap of at least 100% of price and a longer, expressly agreed period aligned with applicable limitation rules**; Buyer must retain meaningful recourse if it does not acquire what it paid for. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud protection is identified. | An effective fraud carve-out across caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure, knowledge, releases and remedy restrictions, preserving non-excludable rights. | **Insert an overriding fraud carve-out and preserve statutory rights**, addressing whose fraud is attributable to Seller; general boilerplate must not shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed in sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, against identified warranties, in a fixed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require specific, fair disclosure plus an indexed archived data room**; document availability is not adequate notice of a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge bar; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal personnel, without imputed or constructive knowledge. | **Delete; fallback to tightly defined actual knowledge applying only to general warranties**, not indemnities or protected claims; “discoverable” effectively makes Buyer insure Seller’s warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, despite outstanding consent and associated conditions. | A Buyer-benefit condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of relevant contractual conditions, without unacceptable amendments, charges or termination rights. | **Make compliant consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions a Completion condition, waivable only by Buyer**, with a long-stop termination right; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Debt repayment and effective security discharge at Completion, supported by lender payoff and release arrangements. | **Require an agreed lender payout statement, direct payment from Seller proceeds and binding simultaneous release mechanics**, with prompt registry discharge evidence; Buyer must not inherit secured debt in a debt-free transaction. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unresolved. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs through explicit price/funds-flow treatment. | **Itemise and allocate these amounts to Seller, verify conditions and on-costs, and provide funding/indemnity for later payment without double counting**; omission risks an undisclosed reduction in Buyer’s acquired value. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; transfer is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, with **AUD 180,000** recorded open. | Verified payment and effective ownership of relevant IP, plus protection against historic ownership defects and associated losses. | **Require payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment/release at or before Completion, backed by a broader specific indemnity outside general limitations**; payment reimbursement alone does not cure defective IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | A completed investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal assessment and compliant remediation/notification, with allocated historic exposure. | **Require investigation deliverables, pre-Completion covenants and a specific indemnity with suitable security; assess a Completion condition if findings warrant**; uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but neither is it a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Verification of aggregate commitment, timing, scope, termination rights, accruals and accounting/price treatment. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and restrict new commitments pending clarification; adjust price only where justified by the agreed mechanics**; neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | All-Claims limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance; time limits apply universally unless excluded. | Expressly differentiated treatment of general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price adjustments and fraud. | **Replace blanket provisions with a category-by-category limitations matrix and express priority rules**; otherwise general boilerplate can defeat separately negotiated protection. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller holding 100%; relied on as evidence of title. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership history, encumbrances, options/convertibles and transfer restrictions, plus complete transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, issuance/transfer documents and relevant searches, and obtain title warranties and releases**; the register alone does not establish an unencumbered, fully transferable 100% interest. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP positions treated as settled under the general regime. | A standalone pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity and tax warranties with appropriate duration; substantive IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. | **Keep both open: negotiate tax-specific protection and separately calibrated IP coverage, including Ironquay**, without allowing general disclosure or thresholds to neutralise specific indemnities; their risk profiles are not adequately addressed by the general regime. |

**Immediate priorities:** resolve Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, bonus funding and Ironquay ownership before Completion; investigate the privacy incident promptly. Separately, do not infer landlord consent or Mossvale consent requirements merely from the lease notification obligation or an assignment restriction.
=== END ADVICE ===
